metaDescription: Six WYBOT cordless pool robots compared: A1, B1, C1, C2, C2 Vision and the S2 Solar, covering filters, navigation, charging and upkeep.
expertTake: The WYBOT C2 is the best all-round pick because its two-stage filter handles both leaves and fine silt. The A1 is the value pick for above-ground pools, and buyers with a small, clean pool should skip the camera and solar models.
introParagraphs: A single brand can cover a pool robot range from simple floor sweepers to camera-guided machines that charge from sunlight. The names are similar, so the differences hide in the filter stack, the navigation method and how the battery gets topped up.

Inside one family, the best choice is usually the cheapest model whose filter and navigation match your pool. Extra intelligence only pays off on awkward layouts, and extra filtration only pays off if you will rinse it.

products.name: WYBOT C2 cordless with 10 and 180 micron filters

specList.label: Filtration
specList.value: 180 micron main stage plus 10 micron fine layer

products.description:
The C2 earns first place for its two-stage filtration. A 180 micron main stage catches leaves, hair and grit, while a 10 micron layer behind it takes the fine dust that clouds water. Most budget robots offer only the coarse stage, so the C2 covers more kinds of mess with one machine.

It climbs walls and steps, which many robots skip, and it connects by Bluetooth rather than depending on a home network. That is a small but real advantage when the pool sits far from the router. Next to the C2 Vision it is the simpler, cheaper machine, since it navigates without a camera.

The fine layer clogs quickly in leaf season, so rinse it after each run and keep the coarse stage clean first. A clogged 10 micron mesh starves the pump and makes the robot look weak. Charge after every cycle and shade the body between uses.
products.bestFor: In-ground pools that collect both leaves and fine silt.
pros: Two-stage filter handles leaves and fine silt together
Climbs walls and steps instead of stopping at the floor
Bluetooth control works without strong home Wi-Fi
Simpler and cheaper than the camera version
cons: Fine mesh layer clogs quickly in leafy conditions
Bluetooth range is shorter than a network link
No camera, so obstacles are found by contact

products.name: WYBOT A1 cordless for above-ground pools

specList.label: Parking
specList.value: Parks itself at the pool edge

products.description:
The A1 is the only machine in this lineup designed around above-ground pools. Above-ground walls are soft and often shallow, so a robot built for them keeps its footprint small and its climbing gentle. The 2,280 GPH pump rating is the lowest here, which fits the smaller volume of water these pools hold.

Its dual-layer filter pairs a 180 micron stage with textured foam, a layout meant to trap fine debris without the heavier clogging of ultra-fine mesh. Self-parking brings it to the edge when the cycle ends, so you are not poking at the water with a hook. Compared with the C1, which advertises both pool types, the A1 is the specialist and the better fit for vinyl liners.

Rinse the foam after every run, because foam holds odor if left damp. Check the pool wall height against the listing before ordering, and dry the body before storage. The brush is the wear part to watch on a vinyl liner.
products.bestFor: Above-ground and vinyl liner pools where wall height and gentleness matter.
pros: Designed around above-ground wall height and liners
Self-parking brings it to the edge after a cycle
Dual-layer filter traps fine debris without ultra-fine clogging
Lowest cost of the family in this lineup
cons: Smallest pump rating, not for large pools
Foam layer holds odor if stored damp
Not intended for deep in-ground walls

products.name: WYBOT B1 cordless with quad-roller brushes
products.description:
The B1 puts its design effort into brushes and weight. Four rollers give more contact area with the floor than a two-roller layout, and they push debris into the intake along the edges where robots usually leave a margin. At 14.3 pounds dry, it is among the easier robots to lift out of the pool, which matters when the body is full of water.

Five cleaning modes let you pick floor-only or full coverage, and path planning keeps the passes tidy. It does not carry the camera of the C2 Vision, so it relies on planned routes and bump sensing. For a pool with a lot of steps, the C2 is the better climber.

Year-three ownership is about the rollers. Four sets of bristles pick up hair and fibres, so cut tangles away every few runs. Rinse the filter and keep the battery out of the sun.
products.bestFor: Owners who struggle with heavy lifting and want good edge cleaning.
pros: Fourteen pound body is easier to lift when wet
Four rollers give more floor contact and edge reach
Five modes cover floor-only and full passes
Path planning keeps coverage tidy
cons: Four rollers collect hair that needs cutting out
Fewer fine-filter options than the C2

products.name: WYBOT C1 cordless 4-in-1 with gyroscope guidance

specList.label: Pool type
specList.value: Aimed at in-ground, above-ground use also listed

products.description:
The C1 runs a dedicated pump motor that is independent of the drive, so suction does not collapse when the robot climbs. A gyroscope tracks heading and keeps its passes in straight lines, which suits rectangular pools. The pump rating of 3,048 GPH sits above the A1 and below the C2's listed figure in this family.

An app lets you tune routes, which gives the C1 flexibility the A1 lacks. Gyro systems drift over long runs, so on a very large pool the lines wander and a few strips get missed. The listing claims both in-ground and above-ground suitability, so confirm the wall height before assuming it works in a shallow vinyl pool.

Upkeep is the standard cordless routine. The same C1 appears in a couple of colour options, so match your filter and brush orders to the exact listing. Rinse the basket every run and check the brush each season.
products.bestFor: Rectangular pools where gyroscope lines give repeatable coverage.
pros: Separate pump motor keeps suction steady on walls
Gyroscope lines suit rectangular pools well
App adds route settings above the A1
Four-in-one coverage handles floor, wall and waterline
cons: Gyro drift can miss strips on large pools
Dual pool-type claims need a wall height check
Fewer filter layers than the C2

products.name: WYBOT C2 Vision with AI camera and HEPA filter

specList.label: Modes
specList.value: Eight modes with custom routes via app

products.description:
A camera is what separates the C2 Vision from the plain C2. It reads the pool, places the robot accurately and lets you draw custom routes in the app, which is most useful on irregular shapes. Eight modes let you tailor passes for floor, walls or targeted areas.

Its filtration swaps the 10 micron layer for a HEPA stage behind a 180 micron basket, a combination aimed at fine dust. Camera systems need a reasonably clear pool, so murky water undermines the mapping. Short of the solar model, this is the most capable machine in the lineup, and also among the most costly.

Wipe the camera window after each run and rinse both filter stages. A HEPA layer is a consumable that loses flow as it clogs, so keep a spare. Charge after use and keep the robot out of direct sun.
products.bestFor: Irregular pools where custom routes and accurate positioning save time.
pros: AI camera positions the robot accurately in odd layouts
App lets you draw custom routes and pick eight modes
HEPA stage behind the basket targets fine dust
Cleans from floor to waterline in one cycle
cons: Camera needs clear water and a clean lens
HEPA layer clogs and needs a spare on hand
Priced above the simpler C2 and C1

products.name: WYBOT S2 Solar Vision with three charging modes

specList.label: Charging
specList.value: Solar panel, DC power or other supply, three modes

products.description:
The S2 is the unusual one: it can recharge from a solar panel in bright sunlight, from a DC supply, or by another connection. That makes it the least dependent on a power outlet near the water. If your pool is far from the house, the solar mode removes an extension cord run.

Solar charging is only as good as your sun, so shaded yards will lean on the DC option. The camera adds self-learning and debris detection, which brings it level with the C2 Vision on intelligence. The cost is the premium tier of the family, and the extra complexity of a panel and charging dock.

Place the panel where it gets direct light and wipe it clean of pollen and dust. Treat the camera and filters like the C2 Vision, and keep the battery out of heat. Check the app schedule after any firmware update.
products.bestFor: Pools far from a power outlet, in a sunny yard.
pros: Solar charging removes the need for a nearby outlet
Three charging modes give flexibility in shade
AI camera recognises debris and learns routes
App scheduling automates daily runs
cons: Solar charging depends on strong sun
Most complex setup with panel and dock

buyingCriteria.explanation: The A1 is built for above-ground pools while the C2 and C2 Vision target in-ground ones. An in-ground robot in a shallow vinyl pool can climb the wrong way and scuff the liner. Check the maker's pool type and wall height before buying. The C1 lists both, but verify with your own wall height.

The C2 uses 10 and 180 micron layers, the C2 Vision pairs a 180 micron basket with HEPA, and the A1 uses 180 micron with foam. Finer mesh catches silt but clogs faster. Pick the stack you will actually rinse. Leaf-heavy pools favour the coarse stage and frequent cleaning.

The C1 uses a gyroscope, the B1 uses path planning, and the C2 Vision and S2 use cameras. Gyroscopes draw straight lines but drift, while cameras map accurately but need clear water. A simple rectangle does not need a camera. An irregular pool does.

Most of the family charges from a wall adapter after each run, but the S2 adds solar and DC modes. Solar helps only with strong sun. Shade or short winter days push you back to the adapter. Decide where the charging point will live.

The B1 is 14.3 pounds dry, which is light for the class. Add the water the body holds on exit and the load is higher. If lifting is hard, weight matters more than pump ratings. Surface parking on the A1 helps too.

The B1 uses four rollers while the C2 uses dual scrubbing brushes. More rollers mean more edge contact but more tangles to clear. Dual brushes are simpler. Check how the brush set is replaced and whether spares are sold.

specDecoder.meaning: The largest particle size a filter layer lets through. A lower micron figure catches finer dirt on the WYBOT filters but clogs sooner.
specDecoder.watchFor: The C2 combines 10 and 180 micron stages, so rinse the fine one after every leaf-heavy run.

specDecoder.meaning: Rated water flow for the pump motor. It signals strength, not cleaning results.
specDecoder.watchFor: The A1 lists 2,280 GPH and the C1 lists 3,048 GPH, so expect the A1 to suit smaller pools.

specDecoder.meaning: Heading tracking that keeps passes straight. It drifts over time and long runs.
specDecoder.watchFor: The C1 relies on it, so large pools may see missed strips.

specDecoder.meaning: A very fine filter stage meant to catch dust-sized particles. It restricts flow quickly if not cleaned.
specDecoder.watchFor: The C2 Vision uses one, so stock a spare.

specDecoder.meaning: A panel feeds the battery in bright light. It supplements, rather than replaces, a wall adapter in most climates.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the S2 offers it, with a DC fallback for shade.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filter design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the layer stack in each model. The C2 with 10 and 180 micron stages set the standard. We rewarded access and replaceability.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pool fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Each WYBOT was tied to the pool surface and shape its listing names. The A1 stood out for above-ground use. We flagged claims that need a wall height check.

howWeEvaluated.title: Navigation
howWeEvaluated.description: We grouped gyroscope, path planning and camera systems. Camera models gained points on irregular pools. We kept simple pools in mind for the cheaper options, because a camera adds cost without adding value on a plain rectangle. We also noted that clear water is a precondition for any vision system.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging and energy
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each robot is powered, including the S2 solar option. We noted dependence on sun and outlets. We kept the reasoning grounded in the listing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We read for weight, brush type and consumables, such as the B1 at 14.3 pounds. WYBOT's listed solar, battery and cleaning-mode details, alongside common owner comments, are the basis for these notes. Lighter and simpler counted for seniors.

cards.label: Gyroscope (C1)
cards.text: Draws straight lines and costs less. It drifts on large pools and finds obstacles by contact. Right for rectangles.

cards.label: Camera (C2 Vision, S2)
cards.text: Maps the pool and recognises debris. It needs clear water and a clean lens. Right for irregular shapes.

howToChoose.note: Rectangle, pick the C1. Irregular pool, pick the C2 Vision.

howToChoose.subheading: For Seniors and Easy Handling Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a light body, simple controls and automatic parking. Lifting a wet robot is the hardest task. Avoid features you will not use.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The B1 at 14.3 pounds is the lightest, and the A1 parks itself at the edge. The C2 adds Bluetooth control without a Wi-Fi setup.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Your pool is irregular, far from an outlet or full of fine dust. The C2 Vision, S2 and C2 solve those problems. Pay for the problem you have.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your pool is small and plain. The A1 or B1 handles it, and the saved money buys a spare filter. Do not pay for cameras you do not need.

maintenance.why: Fine layers clog quickly and starve the pump. A rinse keeps flow steady.
Film from sunscreen blurs vision. Cleaning restores positioning.
Tangles reduce roller grip. They also stall the drive.
Heat and deep discharge age lithium cells. Prompt charging keeps capacity.
Fine mesh stretches and clogs for good. A fresh layer restores flow.

faq.q: Which WYBOT is best for most pools?
faq.a: The C2 covers most in-ground pools with two filter stages and step climbing. Move to the Vision only for irregular shapes, where a camera saves missed corners and wasted cycles. The A1 is the answer for above-ground pools.
Only if the pool is far from an outlet and the yard gets strong sun. Shade pushes you to the DC option. The S2 is a convenience, not a necessity.

faq.q: Does a finer filter clean better?
faq.a: It catches finer dirt but clogs faster. If you will not rinse after every run, a coarse stage cleans more reliably. Match the filter to your habits, and keep a spare layer for the weeks when the pool is dirtiest.

faq.q: Can the C1 work in above-ground pools?
faq.a: The listing says so, but check wall height first. The A1 is designed for the job. Shallow vinyl walls reward the specialist, because the footprint and climb angle are tuned for them.

faq.q: How long will the battery last?
faq.a: Expect good performance for the first seasons, then slow fade. Heat speeds the decline. Treat listed runtime as a new-battery figure.

For route settings and scheduling, yes. The C2 can also be controlled over Bluetooth. Confirm basic modes work without the app before you buy, so a phone update or a dead link never leaves the robot idle.
